subject: Next steps: IAM evidence & compliance items for PulseWell
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Adams <lauren.adams@pulsewell.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@pulsewell.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: IAM evidence & compliance items for PulseWell

Hi Lauren / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the demo earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps from our side to keep the procurement loop moving:

What we covered (short):
- Redwood runtime + Dedicated options for PHI workloads
- Observability & per-route cost/latency dashboards
- IAM integration patterns (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC) and rolling upgrades

Action items I promised to capture:
1) Can you confirm PulseWell’s current SOC 2 status (in-scope, report date, and whether you can share a redacted report)?
2) Do you have specific regulatory constraints (HIPAA / GDPR) for the initial pilot region?
3) For IAM evidence, we typically request: SSO configuration notes (SAML metadata), SCIM provisioning capability, list of admin roles + current RBAC matrix, and an export of admin user accounts if possible. See the checklist I attached below.

If you’re comfortable, please send the items you can share this week. If anything is sensitive we can accept a redacted PDF or provide an IP-restricted S3 upload.

Attachments: redwood_iam_checklist_v1.xlsx (internal checklist — simple mapping to what we’ll need)

Sample suggested timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: you confirm SOC2 status and regs scope
- By Thu 6/21: initial IAM artifacts (SAML metadata, brief RBAC matrix)
- Week of 6/24: security kickoff (30–45m) with our security engineer

I’ll loop in our security/solutions lead for the kickoff once we have a signal from you.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Adams <lauren.adams@pulsewell.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@pulsewell.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:18:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: IAM evidence & compliance items for PulseWell

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear recap and checklist. Quick answers below and I attached what we can share immediately.

SOC 2: We completed SOC 2 Type II in March 2027; we can share a redacted report. I attached a redacted SOC2 cover page and the security controls index (PulseWell_Security_SA_v1.pdf).

Regulatory scope: We are HIPAA-in-scope for the U.S. pilot and GDPR-conscious in EU operations (but pilot will be US).

IAM evidence:
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0. I included our SAML metadata XML as a text block inside the PDF attachment.
- SCIM: Provisioning is supported; our SCIM API requires token-based auth and is currently v2 compatible.
- RBAC: Attached a simple export of admin accounts and roles (PulseWell_ID_Access_Export.csv). The roles CSV has columns: user_email, role_name, org_unit.

We redacted emails of clinicians per privacy policy but included role names. If you need a more complete export for mapping, we can coordinate with our security team.

Attaching: PulseWell_Security_SA_v1.pdf, PulseWell_ID_Access_Export.csv

Next steps: happy to do a kickoff on Friday 6/22 in the afternoon PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Lauren
Director of IT Security | PulseWell Health

Lauren —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments, that’s perfect. We’ll do a quick internal review of the PDF and CSV and get back with any clarifying asks.

Rishi / Marissa — looping you in; key points from PulseWell: SOC2 Type II (Mar 2027), HIPAA in-scope for pilot, SAML + SCIM supported, export attached. Can you please:
- Rishi: validate whether the CSV has enough granularity for RBAC mapping or if we need a scoped export (e.g., system admin usernames).
- Marissa: prep the security kickoff invite and include our security engineer (Samir Khan) + product lead (Daniel Li). Suggest 30–45m.

Lauren — if Friday 6/22 afternoon PT works we’ll accept that and send an invite shortly. If you prefer earlier, let us know.

Best,
Aisha

Thanks for the ping, Aisha / Lauren. Quick read-through: the CSV looks suitable for an initial RBAC mapping — it has role_name and org_unit which we can map to our capability tiers. One clarifying ask: can PulseWell include a sample SAML assertion (redacted) or test SSO metadata endpoint so our infra team can verify attribute mappings (email, groups, is_admin)? If PulseWell prefers not to share an assertion, an attribute mapping table will work.

Marissa — please schedule the 30-minute kickoff for Fri 6/22 2:00–2:30 PM PT (hold tentative) and include: Samir Khan (sec eng), Daniel Li (product), Aisha (solutions), Rishi (security). Lauren / Tom — expect a calendar invite shortly; if that window is bad, propose alternatives.

Lauren — we’ll prepare an initial mapping doc and a short list of integration questions ahead of the call so the meeting can be focused on any gaps.

Cheers,
Rishi
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
